acceptance_criteria.criterion: listBranches() returns both local and remote branches with correct isRemote and isCurrent flags
getCurrentBranch() returns the branch name for a normal checkout and null for detached HEAD
getDefaultBranch() correctly identifies the default branch, falling back from symbolic-ref to checking main/master
createBranch() creates a new branch and switches to it
switchBranch() returns GitResult allowing callers to inspect exit code and stderr for conflict detection
branchExists() correctly differentiates between local-only and remote branch existence
fetchRemote() completes without error for a valid repository with a remote

summary: Created src/git/git-branch.ts with 7 stateless functions: listBranches (parses git branch -a --format into BranchInfo[], filters origin/HEAD symrefs), getCurrentBranch (returns null for detached HEAD), getDefaultBranch (3-step fallback: symref → main → master), createBranch (git checkout -b), switchBranch (git checkout, returns GitResult), branchExists (local refs/heads/ or remote refs/remotes/ lookup), fetchRemote (git fetch [remote]).
Created src/tests/git-branch.test.ts with 19 tests covering all 7 ACs, using a local git fixture with main + extra-branch. All 204 tests pass.

comments.note: src/git/git-branch.ts: getDefaultBranch() makes up to 5 sequential runGit calls in the worst case (symref + 4 verify checks). For most repositories with a configured remote, only 1 call is made. This is acceptable given it's a rarely-invoked utility, but worth noting if it is called in a hot path.

src/git/git-branch.ts: listBranches() uses --format= directly on the CLI args string. If a future callee appends user-supplied content to the format string, it could become an injection vector. Currently safe since the format string is a hardcoded literal.

src/git/git-branch.ts: createBranch() uses `git checkout -b` which is the deprecated form in newer git versions (prefer `git switch -c`). This still works everywhere but may produce deprecation hints in future git releases.

src/tests/git-branch.test.ts: The test for createBranch duplicate detection checks either exitCode !== 0 OR stderr.length > 0. Git actually returns exitCode 1 here, so the check is correct but loose. A stricter assertion on exitCode would be more deterministic.

summary: Reviewed 2 modified files (src/git/git-branch.ts, src/tests/git-branch.test.ts). 0 Critical, 0 High, 2 Medium (missing -- separator in createBranch/switchBranch; no runGit() timeout carried from WP-003), 2 Low. Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: A03/A08 — Medium. src/git/git-branch.ts lines 115 and 127 (createBranch / switchBranch): Neither function inserts a -- separator before the branchName argument. spawn receives ['checkout', '-b', branchName] and ['checkout', branchName] respectively. With shell:false there is no OS-shell injection, but git's own argument parser can still interpret a branchName starting with -- as a flag. Example: switchBranch(path, '--force') executes git checkout --force, which discards uncommitted working-tree changes on the current branch (A08 data integrity). Similarly createBranch(path, '--orphan') would create an orphan without a name. Remediation: insert '--' before branchName in both args arrays: ['checkout', '-b', '--', branchName] and ['checkout', '--', branchName]. This is standard practice to terminate git option processing.

A03 — Low. src/git/git-branch.ts lines 140-142 (branchExists): The ref path is constructed by template literal interpolation: refs/remotes/${remote}/${branchName}. If remote or branchName contains path-traversal segments (e.g. branchName = '../config' yields refs/remotes/origin/../config = refs/remotes/config), git's ref resolution could match an unintended ref, causing branchExists to return true for a non-existent target. shell:false prevents shell execution, but git processes the path itself. Remediation: validate that remote and branchName match a safe refname pattern (e.g. /^[A-Za-z0-9._\-]+$/) before constructing the ref.

A04 — Low. src/git/git-branch.ts listBranches() (line 16): The --format string is a compile-time constant (safe). However, the output is parsed by splitting on \t. Git should never produce branch names or upstream names containing tab characters, but if a malformed git output somehow contained extra tabs the parsing logic (const [refname, head, shortName, upstream] = line.split('\t')) would silently assign extra content to upstream and lose data integrity. Recommendation: validate that each split line produces exactly 4 segments before mapping, or use a more robust format delimiter.

A04 — Medium (carried from WP-003 dependency). src/git/git-cli.ts runGit(): No timeout on the spawned process. This affects all 7 functions in git-branch.ts. fetchRemote() is the highest-risk caller: a blocked SSH connection or slow remote can hang the process indefinitely. Recommendation: add AbortController-based timeout to runGit().

summary: FAIL — one Blocking issue. createBranch() and switchBranch() lack the -- argument separator before branchName, allowing a branchName value starting with -- to be interpreted by git as a flag rather than a branch name. switchBranch(path, '--force') executes git checkout --force, which discards all uncommitted working-tree changes while returning exit code 0 — a silent data loss scenario. The Blocking fix requires both source changes and new test coverage. All other code quality dimensions are sound: the function structure is clean, stateless, and follows the established project conventions for args-array construction and GitResult contract."

comments.note: BLOCKING — src/git/git-branch.ts createBranch() line: args array ['checkout', '-b', branchName] has no -- separator before branchName. A branchName value starting with -- is parsed by git as a flag, not a branch name. Example: createBranch(path, '--orphan') executes git checkout --orphan without a branch name argument, creating an orphan branch with no commits. Fix: change to ['checkout', '-b', '--', branchName].

BLOCKING — src/git/git-branch.ts switchBranch() line: args array ['checkout', branchName] has no -- separator before branchName. Critical case: switchBranch(path, '--force') executes git checkout --force, which discards ALL uncommitted working-tree changes on the current branch and returns exit code 0 — the caller receives a successful GitResult while user data has been irreversibly destroyed. Fix: change to ['checkout', '--', branchName].

BLOCKING — src/tests/git-branch.test.ts lacks test coverage for the -- separator fix. After the Blocking fix is applied, add at least one test verifying that a branchName starting with '--' (e.g. '--force') returns a non-zero exit code and does NOT modify the working tree. Without a regression test, the fix can be silently reverted in future refactors.

src/git/git-branch.ts: createBranch(), switchBranch(), and fetchRemote() are all declared async but never use await — they simply return runGit() directly. This is the same convention violation corrected by the Reviewer in WP-003 (cloneRepository). Drop the async keyword from all three functions to align with the established non-async pattern of runGit() in git-cli.ts. Non-behavioral change — return types are unchanged.

src/git/git-branch.ts fetchRemote(): the remote parameter has the same potential flag-interpretation issue — fetchRemote(path, '--all') would execute git fetch --all (fetching all remotes) rather than failing with 'no such remote'. This is lower severity than the checkout cases (no data loss path), but consider adding '--' before remote: ['fetch', '--', remote] when remote is provided. Note that git does support 'git fetch -- origin' syntax.

summary: Rework addressing the two Blocking items from the code-review bounce.

BLOCKING FIX 1 (createBranch flag injection): The reviewer/auditor recommended adding '--' before branchName in the args array. However, 'git checkout -b -- branchName' is semantically broken — git treats '--' as the branch name and branchName as the start-point, producing 'fatal: branch -- cannot be created'. The correct fix is input validation: createBranch() and switchBranch() now return Promise.resolve({exitCode:128, ...}) for any branchName starting with '-'. This is correct because git check-ref-format forbids ref names starting with '-', so the validation is git-semantically accurate and does not break any legitimate use.

BLOCKING FIX 2 (switchBranch flag injection): 'git checkout -- branchName' was equally broken — it treats branchName as a pathspec (file restore), not a branch. Same input-validation guard applied: early return with exitCode 128 and informative stderr for any name starting with '-'.

REGRESSION TESTS: Added two new tests in git-branch.test.ts — (1) createBranch with '--force' returns exitCode 128 and does not modify HEAD or current branch; (2) switchBranch with '--force' returns exitCode 128 and does not discard staged changes. Both tests pass.

CONVENTION FIX: Dropped async from createBranch(), switchBranch(), and fetchRemote() — they never used await and now correctly match the non-async pattern established in git-cli.ts and fixed in WP-003.
All 206 tests pass (up from 204: 2 new regression tests).

comments.note: The proposed fix from both the Security Auditor and Reviewer (insert '--' before branchName in git checkout args arrays) is semantically incorrect for 'git checkout'. For 'git checkout -b -- branchName', git consumes '--' as the branch name and treats branchName as the start-point. For 'git checkout -- branchName', git treats branchName as a pathspec for file restoration. The correct mitigation is input validation rejecting names starting with '-', which is also semantically accurate since git check-ref-format forbids such names. The downstream agents should be aware that the '--' pattern is only safe for 'git switch --' (not 'git checkout'), if the project ever migrates to 'git switch' in future WPs.

src/git/git-branch.ts: The same '-' prefix guard should ideally be applied to branchExists() branchName and remote parameters, and to fetchRemote() remote parameter, to prevent flag injection through those paths. These are out of scope for this rework but noted for a future cleanup pass.

comments.note: A03 — Low. src/git/git-branch.ts line 162: branchExists() constructs the remote ref by template literal interpolation — `refs/remotes/${remote}/${branchName}`. Neither remote nor branchName is validated against a safe refname pattern. With shell:false there is no OS-level injection, but a branchName of '../config' yields refs/remotes/origin/../config which git resolves as refs/remotes/config, potentially producing an incorrect true result for a non-existent branch. Developer noted this guard is out of scope for this rework. Recommended: validate both parameters match /^[A-Za-z0-9._\-]+$/ before constructing the ref.

A03 — Low. src/git/git-branch.ts line 179: fetchRemote() passes the optional remote parameter directly as a git argument with no prefix guard — fetchRemote(path, '--all') executes git fetch --all (fetching all remotes) instead of failing. Developer explicitly noted this case as out of scope for this rework. Recommended: add the same startsWith('-') guard used in createBranch/switchBranch's before passing remote to runGit.

A04 — Medium (carried from WP-003). src/git/git-cli.ts runGit(): No AbortController-based timeout on the spawned git process. All seven functions in git-branch.ts inherit this gap. fetchRemote() is the highest-risk caller: a blocked SSH handshake or unreachable remote can hang the process indefinitely. Remediation: add a configurable timeout to runGit() using AbortController + setTimeout so callers can bound fetch operations.

src/tests/git-branch.test.ts: createBranch duplicate-detection test uses a loose assertion (assert.ok(result.exitCode !== 0 || result.stderr.length > 0)). This can hide a theoretical regression where git switches to an already-existing branch with exitCode 0 and no stderr. Tightening to assert.notStrictEqual(result.exitCode, 0) would be more deterministic. Non-blocking; the current behavior is practically correct.
